Vs.

full_judgment: 10. The further contention of the learned Additional Attorney-General that the High Court Division was in error in not holding that the writ petition was not maintainable since the respondent did not avail of the remedy available under section 33 of the Act. This contention of the learned Additional Attorney-General is not well founded since the said section provides for refund of duties or charges said to have been paid or over paid through inadvertent error or misdirection’s if applied within the time specified in the said section. There is no such case as to realisation of duties and other levies from the respondent as against the goods imported from India through Benapole. Furthermore, question of limitation as provided in sub-section (2) of section 33 of the Act as regard claim in respect of duties paid in the case of provisional assessment under section 81 of the Act has no manner of application in the instant case since there was no final assessment. So, in no way provision of section 33 of the Act disentitles the respondent to seek direction for refund of excess duties realised at the time of provisional assessment of duties on the goods imported from India through Benapole and, as such, High Court Division has committed no error in making the direction for refund of the excess duties and other levies realised by the customs authorities upon making assessment under section 81 of the Act. Had the customs authorities made the assessment final within the reasonable time and that thereupon if the respondent would have been entitled to refund and that would have not approached the customs authority only then there could have been a case as provided by sub-section (2) of section 33 of the Act. But the said situation is totally absent in the instant case.
